description: Three hooks. (1) PreToolUse on ExitPlanMode — Plan Briefing checkpoint: a deterministic, stateless Node command hook on EVERY ExitPlanMode (Quick Fix Mode, /create-spec & /update-spec plan phases, and plain plan mode). It allows when a real user reply precedes the call — skipping the agent's mechanical tool turns (e.g. the ToolSearch that loads a deferred ExitPlanMode, a post-approval Edit) so they do not break the check — and blocks a straight planning -> ExitPlanMode skip with a short reminder. The check is anchored to the current plan session: a first pass finds where plan mode was (re-)entered — an EnterPlanMode tool call, or a genuine transition into plan read from a real user message's own permissionMode field (the reliable signal for a manual shift+tab re-entry after a restart drops plan-mode state) — then a second pass walks back only to that boundary, so a deny never points at stale text from a previous plan session or from before a restart. Crucially, a bare permission-mode:plan marker seen WHILE ALREADY in plan is ignored, not treated as a boundary: Claude Code writes one at essentially every plan-mode turn boundary, and the old logic mistook those for a fresh re-entry and false-blocked the compliant briefed-then-replied flow whenever a routine marker sat between the reply and the exit. Fail-open on any uncertainty, so it never deadlocks. Filters subagent (isSidechain) and injected (isMeta) entries. Reads the transcript only; writes nothing anywhere. (2) SessionStart on startup/resume — injects a short reminder (session-start-skill-reminder.js) to load and use the spec-driven-development skill for any code work. Static context injection, no project detection: the reminder itself states the 'if this is a code project' condition and lets the agent judge. Writes nothing. (3) PreToolUse on SendMessage — executor session longevity checkpoint: a subagent is resumed by messaging it, so counting prior SendMessage calls sharing the same `to` in the transcript yields that session's round count with no state file. Measured across real transcripts, a median executor session takes ~10-15 resumes while the tail reaches 119 and 105 on a single subagent — long past the point where the session's context is mostly a record of its own earlier reasoning rather than the current task (the anchoring the convergence fuse already guards against by spawning fresh eyes at Round 5). It injects additionalContext and nothing else — at resume #15 a soft note, from #25 a firmer one — and emits no permissionDecision on either, so the call always passes through untouched and the hook can never block, prompt, or alter it. Deliberately not a gate: whether the session holds tacit knowledge a fresh spawn would lose is visible only to the main agent, so a permission prompt would put that question to the user, who sees only a hex id and a count. What the main agent lacks is not judgment but the count itself — its context has no record of how many times it has resumed a session — so the hook supplies the fact, review-protocol.md supplies the criterion, and the main agent decides. Reviewer sessions are deliberately not exempt (a long reviewer is exactly what the fuse treats as suspect, and its corpus re-reads cheaply from disk); the threshold is far above a normal review loop. Filters isSidechain entries so a subagent's own dispatches never count. Fail-open on any parse/shape error, a missing transcript, or a SendMessage with no `to` (e.g. a peer-session message). Reads stdin + the transcript only; writes nothing.
